requirements.requirement: os-comparison-worker runs on node1 as a managed service named inventory-worker
requirements.summary: A systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service was created with ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker, loaded via daemon-reload, and confirmed active (running) both immediately after creation and after the subsequent reboot.

requirements.requirement: Service runs under a dedicated inventorysvc account
requirements.summary: A system account inventorysvc (uid 999, nologin shell, no home) was created via useradd --system, the unit file sets User=inventorysvc/Group=inventorysvc, and ps output both pre- and post-reboot shows the running worker process owned by inventorysvc (PID 2920 then PID 837).

requirements.requirement: Service is enabled so it starts automatically (managed service expectation)
requirements.summary: systemctl enable --now was run, is-enabled reported 'enabled' before reboot, and after a full reboot the service was again enabled and active without manual intervention, demonstrating persistence across restarts.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (8336c3a1...) and active/enabled service with inventorysvc ownership were captured, systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged, the node became briefly unreachable (connection refused), then came back reachable with a different boot_id (39510b7f...) and a later uptime -s value, and the service was reconfirmed active, enabled, and running as inventorysvc post-restart. The fixed lifecycle snapshots corroborate the same boot-identity transition and show no failed systemd units or package-health regressions after the restart.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied the core task: os-comparison-worker runs as the systemd-managed service inventory-worker under the dedicated inventorysvc system account on node1, verified via unit file content and process ownership. The independent restart-evidence protocol was also fully and directly demonstrated — pre-restart baseline, reboot acknowledgement, transient unreachability, a changed boot_id, and confirmed post-restart recovery of the service under the correct account — corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Only a minor, low-risk leftover file (/tmp/err) from the reboot-polling loop was left behind.
limitations: Reliance on ps/systemctl output as reported by the executor's own shell session rather than an independently triggered probe, though corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshot boot-identity cross-check.
No evidence was captured on data persistence beyond service state, but the task/service itself is stateless (a sleep loop), so this is not a material gap.

operational_hygiene.summary: Commands were mostly read-only discovery, purposeful configuration, or bounded verification. One early useradd attempt (cmd-4fb1d3f84e124eae) failed with permission denied and made no state change, immediately corrected by rerunning with sudo (cmd-83dc16e89e464524) — not a hygiene issue. The boot-identity polling loop after reboot (cmd-006c7a7019134bd9) redirected stderr to /tmp/err, which persisted as a small leftover diagnostic file visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot; this is a low-risk, unreverted residue rather than a broad or destructive mutation. No failed services, no unsafe exposure (no listening sockets), and no package-health regressions were observed after the executor's work.
